_comment: Benchmark constants v3. The reference numbers the build still reads, after the quartile-lever model was retired on 2026-09-23 (docs/DATA_MODEL.md #3): the basket of comparable launches is the benchmark for every volume and rate. What stays: order_split (the medians split a display group's target across its raw channels, since the panel is grouped), cost_per_purchase (the Median is the default price of a paid unit; a release can type its own), the entry-to-order rates, cannibalisation 0.2 (the LE standard per the workbook's spend rules), the framing defaults, the budget sense check, the spend rules and the cost-curve priors. Transcribed from the 2026-08-28 LAUNCH PERFORMANCE OVERVIEW (recomputed panel; quartiles over the historical release panel). See docs/DATA_MODEL.md #4 for provenance. Currency EUR: the spend and the prices these were computed from are Meta's and Shopify's euro figures.

order_split._meaning: channel share of unadjusted draw+preorder units, Low=P25 / Medium=median / High=P75; the build reads the Medium column only, renormalised inside each display group, to split a group's basket target across its channels

cost_per_purchase._meaning: EUR per paid unit, quartiles over the paid campaigns on file; Median is the default the paid budget is priced at when a release has no cost_per_purchase of its own

spend_rules.cpe_daily_drift_note: Retired 2026-09-28: cost per entry no longer drifts with the calendar. It rises with the campaign's spend so far (cpe_wearout), which the 2026-09-28 fit on 47 campaigns / 783 campaign-days preferred to a straight drift a day (deviance 1375 against 1456; the straight drift read 3.6% a day). The workbook's 5/7/10% a day by third is kept in cpe_daily_drift_by_third_workbook for reference: it is the cost rise along the workbook's own ramping spend path, which the spend-so-far curve now prices.
spend_rules._source: The cumulative-ROI bands (0.9 / 1.3), the 30% cap and the 10% dead band are the TL template's 'ROI / SPEND RULES - DO NOT CHANGE' block (LAUNCH PERFORMANCE OVERVIEW, TL_Template rows 416-428), applied to LE for want of a fuller LE block. The LE template's own SPEND RULES (rows 284-299) are: decrease/increase steps of 10%, max increase per day 2.0, target ROI AA 1.1, a 30% decrease on a zero-conversion day, a 100% decrease (pause) after 3 days of zero conversion, and 'Expected Increase in Spend (%)' 5/7/10 by third - a typed constant with no derivation, read by row 206 as the daily growth of the forecast cost per unit. Neither tab derives its drift from data; the TL tab labels its 2.16%/day '(assumed)'.

cpe_spend_elasticity_note: Prior for the within-campaign elasticity of cost per entry to the day's budget, net of the wear-out on spend so far. Poisson fit with one level per campaign on every Meta draw campaign tied to a release, 47 campaigns / 783 campaign-days with spend over 20 (etl/analysis/cpe_elasticity.py, 2026-09-28): 0.094 +/- 0.037. Per-campaign fits spread with a between-campaign sd of 0.08 (cpe_spend_elasticity_sd), the prior's width. With a calendar-day drift in its place the same data read 0.38: most of what looked like the price of a bigger day is the spend adding up, which cpe_wearout now carries. A campaign with cpe_fit_min_days of history gets its own elasticity fitted and shrunk to this prior by precision (etl/build.py campaign_cost_terms). Doubling the day's budget makes an entry about 6% dearer at 0.09. Set to 0 to price the day's level flat.
cpe_wearout_note: Prior for the wear-out w: each doubling of what a campaign has spent so far makes its next entry 2^w times dearer, read as (1 + spend so far / cpe_wearout_k)^w. Same fit (etl/analysis/cpe_elasticity.py, 2026-09-28, 47 campaigns / 783 campaign-days): 0.223 +/- 0.019, an entry 17% dearer (14% fewer entries a euro) with each doubling; between-campaign sd 0.18 (cpe_wearout_sd). K = EUR 100: the fit is flat below it and worsens above (deviance 1375 at 100, 1414 at 1,000). The exploratory fits on the sign-ups the draw campaigns bring and on link clicks across every campaign, sign-up campaigns included, wear out alike (17% and 14% fewer a euro per doubling). A campaign with cpe_fit_min_days of history gets its own wear-out fitted and shrunk to this prior by precision (etl/build.py campaign_cost_terms).
cpe_growth_factor_note: Superseded: the forward cost per entry follows the campaign's spend so far (cpe_wearout) and the day's budget (cpe_spend_elasticity), one path for the paid projection, the ROI chart, the budget and the ROI floor (etl/build.py CostPath). Kept for reference only.
